summary: Round 19 plan check, 17:31-17:55Z, files only (no Kaggle calls). The finals are still #37 + #38. Probes 45 and 46 are PENDING at the 17:23:29Z header (45 L > 6.13 h, 8.0 h mark 19:15:12Z; 46 L > 2.77 h, 8.0 h mark 22:36:59Z). E10 RUN 5 at 16:44Z found 0 signals; we are CSV rank 287, SubmissionCount 46. No rule was broken in the 16:08-17:21Z entries. Six things need attention before 00:05Z. (1) The round focus says 'round 18 said only N1 is cheap', but round 18 REFUTED N1 (R18NL-1), and the main session's own card R18-A1 (6) says 'no N1/N2 build before the deadline'. Building N1 tonight breaks a pre-registered line and needs a new user OK. (2) The branch table has no row for '46 still PENDING at the W1 cutoff'. 46's dummy ran 24% slower, so its 9.0 h mark (23:36:59Z) is right at 23:45Z. (3) The W1 files exp76c, exp76e and exp76g are not built, and exp73m has no dummy. The GPU queue held exp75 for 4 h, so these dummies must go out speculatively now, not after the reads. (4) The fallback in the 17:21Z entry (exp76a -> exp75) contradicts the card (exp76a -> exp72 -> exp75). The card's chain can put two secFT files (exp76d + exp72) in W1. (5) The CI runtime is underestimated. The dummy mean is 158 s/video, so the hidden run needs 2.2-2.85 h and L(exp76a) is ~9.8-10.45 h, not 9.6-9.8 h. The card's rule for the CI insertion gate subtracts the upper CI bound, which is anti-conservative. (6) Round-18 actions R18-A2 (RESUME POINT, MEMORY) and R18-A5 (ledger families) are still undone, and ladder_watch.py cannot be 'restarted with new args' (R18-A8) because its refs and base count are hardcoded. Also verified: the exp76a/exp76d notebook shas match CONTEXT, their diffs vs exp70b hold only the intended lines, and exp75's CI moved 64.6% of nodes with 0 duplicate positions. The UP test for 45/46 can use the hourly E10 snapshots, which already hold TeamId and SubmissionCount, but S0 must be picked by SubmissionCount, not by time.

findings.what: The CI runtime is underestimated, and the card's CI insertion-gate reading is anti-conservative. The exp75 dummy log gives per-video CI times of 120.9 / 77.5 / 195.4 / 238.0 s (mean 158 s; roughly linear in detections: 9k -> 78 s, 81k -> 238 s). For 100-130 hidden videos, that is 50-65 videos per worker x 158 s = 2.2-2.85 h, not '~100 videos / 2 GPUs x ~150 s = ~2.1 h'. So L(exp76a) is ~7.58 + (2.2..2.85) = ~9.8-10.45 h, not 9.6-9.8 h. exp76a submitted at 00:05Z scores ~09:50-10:35Z. Card (3) reads the insertion gate on 'L_hi minus the CI stage (... up to 65 videos per worker)'. Subtracting the upper CI bound (2.85 h) makes 'did NOT fire' look proven up to L_hi 10.85 h, beyond the 10.75 h admission ceiling, so the gate can never read open. For exp76c (exp70q base, +24% K2 part), the CI budget is 10.5 h minus the K2 part. If 46's L_hi > 9.0 h, CI covers only ~60% or less of the videos.

Copying exp75's gate ('nodes/forks/edges identical to K2 121,252 / 75 / 117,077') would FALSE-FAIL exp76a, because exp70b has 74 forks and 117,076 edges.
